summary: Jesus warns disciples that stumbling blocks will come but causing a vulnerable person to fall is grave; repeated repentance must meet repeated forgiveness. When apostles ask for more faith, Jesus speaks of mustard-seed trust and then corrects entitlement through servants who have only done their assigned duty. Traveling between Samaria and Galilee, he cleanses ten men with skin disease as they go to priests; only a Samaritan returns, praising God and giving thanks, and Jesus says his faith has saved him. Asked when God's kingdom comes, Jesus rejects observable countdowns and says it is ‘within’ or ‘among’ them. He then speaks of the Son of Man's suffering, sudden disclosure, Noah and Lot, attachment to possessions, and a separation impossible to manage by advance signs.
whyItMatters: Community life needs fierce protection of the vulnerable, inexhaustible restoration, and service without claims on God. Gratitude exposes the outsider who truly perceives grace, while kingdom expectation is pulled away from spectacle toward Jesus's present activity and a future revelation no timetable can domesticate.

outline.heading: Stumbling, rebuke, repentance, and repeated forgiveness
Mustard-seed faith and servants without entitlement

keyVerses.text: Even so you also, when you have done all the things that are commanded you, say, ‘We are unworthy servants. We have done our duty.’”
keyVerses.why: Obedience is vocation, not leverage that makes God indebted to the disciple.

keyVerses.text: Then he said to him, “Get up, and go your way. Your faith has healed you.”
keyVerses.why: The same Greek salvation verb reaches beyond cleansing toward grateful, relational wholeness.

keyVerses.text: neither will they say, ‘Look, here!’ or, ‘Look, there!’ for behold, God’s Kingdom is within you.”
keyVerses.why: The ambiguous phrase is better heard against a plural audience and the kingdom-bearing presence of Jesus.

questions.question: What is a stumbling block?
questions.answer: Skandalon is a trigger, trap, or obstacle that causes someone to fall. Jesus says offenses are inevitable in a damaged world but never excuses the person who creates them, especially for a ‘little one.’ Community forgiveness therefore begins with protection and truthful rebuke, not silence around harm.

questions.question: Does forgiving seven times mean tolerating repeated abuse?
questions.answer: The saying joins rebuke, repentance, and forgiveness. It forbids nursing vengeance against a person who returns while not erasing boundaries, consequences, or protection of the vulnerable. Forgiveness releases retaliation; reconciliation and restored trust require truth and safety.

questions.question: Why doesn't Jesus simply grant ‘more faith’?
questions.answer: He shifts from quantity to the efficacy of even seed-small trust. The mulberry image is deliberate exaggeration about what reliance on God can do, not a magic technique for landscape commands. The next servant saying then prevents powerful faith from becoming spiritual entitlement.

questions.question: Does ‘unworthy servants’ mean people have no value?
questions.answer: The adjective can mean without claim to special credit or merely doing what was owed. Jesus is correcting a transactional posture in which obedience obligates the master. Elsewhere Luke insists people are valued by God; this image attacks merit-based entitlement, not human dignity.

questions.question: Why send the ten to priests before they are clean?
questions.answer: Priests could verify cleansing and restore participation under Torah. The men act on Jesus's command while still visibly afflicted and are cleansed ‘as they went.’ The route joins trust, lawful reintegration, and healing; it does not portray priestly process as opposed to Jesus.

questions.question: What is the difference between the ten being cleansed and one being ‘saved’?
questions.answer: All ten receive bodily cleansing. The Samaritan returns, glorifies God, gives thanks, and is told his faith has sōzō-ed him — saved, healed, or made whole. Luke distinguishes gift received from gift recognized in worship and relationship without implying the other nine became physically diseased again.

questions.question: Does ‘the kingdom is within you’ mean only an inner spiritual state?
questions.answer: Entos hymōn can mean within you or in your midst/among you. Jesus is answering plural Pharisees, whom Luke hardly presents as inwardly possessing the kingdom, while he himself stands and acts among them. An interior dimension is possible, but the immediate sense likely points to God's reign already present in Jesus beyond their observational categories.

questions.question: Are the people ‘taken’ rescued in a rapture?
questions.answer: Luke compares the day with Noah and Lot, where sudden judgment overtakes ordinary life, then warns against turning back like Lot's wife. The text never labels taken or left as the saved group, and the disciples' ‘Where?’ receives an ominous corpse-and-vultures image. Building a rapture sequence from these verbs exceeds the passage.
